title: Post-incident remediation: tenant tail-latency isolation and reservation hysteresis
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-03-04 evening peak we observed a sustained tail-latency degradation for several Dedicated clusters serving production tenants. Symptoms: long tail latencies (p99+ spikes to >2.5s for token generation), tenant eviction-like slowdowns, and increased pod churn in the reservation autoscaler. Impact: 7 paying tenants experienced degraded request success rates; two customers raised support tickets reporting timeouts.

Primary contributing factors (consolidated from telemetry and logs):
- Reservation mis-sizing: the reservation autoscaler aggressively shrank tenant reservations when observed utilization dipped briefly (hysteresis too tight). This caused immediate resource contention when bursty tenants returned, producing queuing and latency spikes.
- Noisy-neighbor burst behavior: several tenants simultaneously consumed burst tokens (policy allows large short-term bursts), overwhelming node-level CPU and memory headroom.
- KV/cache thrash: heavy prefix churn caused elevated KV cache miss rates and larger-than-expected memory pressure on inference workers, amplifying latency.
- Insufficient locality for fallbacks: smart routing fell back to compatible model variants but routing latency and cold KV caches increased cost of fallback.

Immediate mitigation taken (during incident):
- Emergency soft-increase of reservations for affected clusters (manual override) to stabilize throughput and reduce queuing.
- Temporary tightening of per-tenant concurrent request caps to limit impact of any single noisy tenant.
- Opened support channel with top-affected customers; extra credits and monitoring were offered.

Proposed remediation plan (3-phase):
Phase A (short-term, safety-focused, target release runtime-1.21):
  1) Implement reservation hysteresis window: require at least a 10-minute stable low-utilization period before auto-shrinking reservations. Rationale: prevents oscillation from transient dips. Owner: Miguel. Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-19.
  2) Introduce per-tenant burst ceiling and short-term fairness throttle: cap burst token drain to a percentage of the tenant's reservation over 30s windows. Owner: Priya Kaur. Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-18.
  3) Rapid KV cache telemetry: add per-tenant cache hit/miss metrics and alerts for >20% miss-rate sustained for 5m. Owner: Jin Park. Estimate: 2 points. Due: 2026-03-12.

Phase B (mid-term, automation and safety nets):
  1) Autoscaler soft-reserve policy: prefer keeping a fractional buffer (e.g., +15% headroom) when cluster-wide burst probability is high (calculated from historical burst patterns). Product trade-off: slightly higher steady-state allocation vs fewer incidents. Owner: Miguel + ML infra. Estimate: 5 points. Due: 2026-04-02.
  2) Tenant isolation modes: add a 'constrain-on-noise' mode where noisy tenants are placed into reduced CPU-share cgroups and deprioritized on shared GPUs until they cool down. Owner: SRE team (Harper Stone). Estimate: 8 points. Due: 2026-04-09.

Phase C (long-term, instrumentation and policy refinement):
  1) Simulation harness: nightly synthetic replay of burst workload distributions to validate autoscaler and burst policy under a range of scenarios. Owner: Research (Eval infra). Estimate: 8 points. Due: 2026-05-01.
  2) Rollout plan & runbook: update postmortem and runbooks with clear on-call steps and an automated playbook for manual overrides. Owner: Aisha. Estimate: 2 points. Due: 2026-03-26.

Trade-offs considered and rationale: 
- Hysteresis window length: chose 10m after simulating oscillation patterns; shorter windows still risk thrash, longer windows increase idle cost.
- Burst ceilings vs customer experience: applying per-tenant burst ceilings prevents single-tenant storms but could limit legitimate short spikes; rollout will start with conservative ceilings and be tuned with customer telemetry.
- Soft-reserve buffer increases steady cost but reduces incident probability; propose to tie buffer policy to region and customer tier to minimize cost impact.

Action items (concrete):
- ENG-55801-A: Implement reservation hysteresis (Miguel) — 3pt — due 2026-03-19 — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287 (WIP).
- ENG-55801-B: Add burst ceiling enforcement and extend token-bucket tests (Priya) — 3pt — due 2026-03-18 — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2143 (draft).
- ENG-55801-C: Per-tenant KV cache metrics/alerts (Jin) — 2pt — done 2026-03-12 — Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/kv-cache/tenant-hit-miss
- ENG-55801-D: Canary rollout plan + runbook updates (Aisha) — 2pt — due 2026-03-26 — Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Reservation+Hysteresis+Runbook
- ENG-55801-E: SRE isolation mode design doc (Harper) — 8pt — due 2026-04-09 — Doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-noise-isolation

Acceptance criteria (for close):
- No repeat of tail-latency incidents for same class of workload in 14 days after rolling out hysteresis & burst ceilings.
- Dashboards show reduced KV miss-induced memory pressure and lower p99 latency under equivalent burst tests.
- Canary customers report no functional regressions and acceptable latency under capped burst conditions.
